critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1165 lines. Splitting into routers/security/services modules is overdue.

startup_setup calls db.admin_sessions.create_index('expires_at_ttl', expireAfterSeconds=0) but the actual field is 'expires_at' (string ISO date). This TTL index is a NO-OP because (a) it indexes a non-existent field and (b) TTL indexes require BSON Date type, not ISO strings. Sessions will accumulate forever unless manually cleaned. Fix: store expires_at as datetime object and index the correct field name. Currently mitigated by verify_admin deleting expired sessions on access, but stale sessions never accessed will linger.
Same TTL concern for db.login_attempts — no TTL cleanup on locked_until, so old records linger (mostly harmless since keyed by IP with unique index).
_check_brute_force compares string ISO dates via datetime.fromisoformat — works because created via .isoformat() but fragile. Consider storing as native datetime.

Rate-limit key uses _client_ip which trusts X-Forwarded-For header without validation. In production behind a trusted proxy this is fine; if backend ever becomes directly reachable, attackers can bypass all rate limits by rotating XFF header (which our own tests exploit intentionally).

sanitize_text uses bleach.clean(text, tags=[], strip=True) then re.sub(r'\s+', ' ') — safe. But max_len is applied AFTER sanitization, so if a user submits long HTML, they'd get less usable text than expected. Minor UX issue.
HTTPS/HSTS is gated on ENABLE_HTTPS_ONLY=false in .env. Remind user to flip this to 'true' on Hostinger once SSL is provisioned.
CORS_ORIGINS='*' in .env - MUST be tightened to actual domain(s) before production launch, otherwise credentials-mode requests will be blocked AND any origin can hit the API.
